confirmatory.why: the R2-BRIDGE/R2-11/R2-12 primary budget: links R3-04 to the original negative R2-12 result under the corrected runtime and gives a middle point of the budget gradient. Descriptive N=6 (one full permutation cycle); no classification label.

negative_control.caution: the real runtime at 8 GiB still has eviction (victim_calls 7966 in R3-03B) so 'zero retention benefit' is a replay-level expectation that the mechanism phase checks directly
negative_control.why: replay retention benefit is exactly zero (tie): P-S should equal only the extra policy bookkeeping time and miss/eviction counters should tie. It validates that the instrument does not manufacture a retention effect, and its S-A contrast is the budget R3-03B already measured (replication check). Descriptive N=6.

primary.limit: A NET_LOSS at 1.5 GiB is not a proof of loss at budgets that were not tested; it bounds the tested implementation at the most favourable tested budget.
primary.why: largest evidence-supported retention benefit (R2-11 replay: 0.131% miss-byte reduction vs 0.037% at 4 GiB and exactly 0 at 8 GiB); it is the best case for NET_WIN: if the real policy cannot recover its bookkeeping cost where retention helps most, no other tested budget can win. It also never had a real-model conformance for any policy in the corrected runtime, so the mechanism phase covers it first.

prior_evidence_use.budget_selection: R2-11 per-budget replay retention deltas (replay evidence, used as a prior only)
prior_evidence_use.not_used_as_observations: all R2-12 and R3-03B outcome values
prior_evidence_use.positive_control: none claimed: no direct runtime positive control exists for retention benefit
prior_evidence_use.variance_planning: R2-12 paired-delta SD (conservative proxy) and R3-03B block SD (check)

rejected: 1.5+4+8 all as primary (multiplicity, ~3x cost, no information gain for the single net question)
8 GiB only (would test the budget where retention benefit is zero; cannot answer 'does retention pay for itself')
4 GiB only (small effect, I/O-bound noise, no best-case test)
